title: Keep the Discussion Moving When It Gets Stuck
status: New proposed complete Lesson07 production script, continuing the accepted visual and delivery conventions.
continuity: L01 introduced shared discussion; L02 developed reasons; L03 listening and connected responses; L04 constructive disagreement; L05 task interpretation; L06 personal experience and follow-ups. L07 now practises restoring useful discussion when a pause, overlap, unbalanced participation or sidetrack needs attention.
boundaries: Seven independently editable sections, not seven additional lessons.
Observe the immediate conversation before choosing a small useful intervention; waiting can be appropriate.
No universal silence threshold, compulsory leader, equal-turn quota or formula that guarantees a response.
Independent excerpts reset; behaviour in one example does not define a character personality.
A question about an activity is not evidence that participants have learned its answer.
20 minutes is the fictional welcome activity length, not a speaking, discussion or course deadline.
Silent overlap illustrations do not test hearing or detect real interruptions.
Practice remains authored and unrecorded. Model viewing cannot establish speech, repair success or consensus.
Final localized explanation, recorded English dialogue, overlap mixing and measured audio alignment belong to the later pass.

sections.title: Notice What the Discussion Needs
sections.learningOutcome: Use observable words and turn-taking to identify a small next need; distinguish an unfinished task connection from assumed agreement, ignorance, hostility or a permanent participant trait.

sections.title: Restart After a Pause
sections.learningOutcome: Use a pause after a proposal as a context to observe and respond to, without inferring agreement or a motive; compare a focused open question with a premature decision or pressured invitation.

sections.title: Handle Overlapping Turns
sections.learningOutcome: Resolve an overlap by making room for a turn and preserving an unfinished point, without assuming hostile intent, treating turn-taking permission as agreement or combining proposals before they are understood.

sections.title: Invite a Contribution Without Pressure
sections.learningOutcome: Offer a relevant invitation that leaves the other person free to contribute, pass or come in later, without inferring motives or assigning equal speaking quotas.

sections.title: Bring a Sidetrack Back to the Task
sections.learningOutcome: Check whether a side topic contributes to the stated task, then redirect to a specific unresolved issue without dismissing creative ideas or inventing a discussion deadline.

sections.title: Rehearse a Small Repair
sections.learningOutcome: Privately rehearse one task-linked next move after a brief pause, leaving space for the actual reply and avoiding claims that the plan or discussion is already resolved.

sections.title: Choose the Next Move in a New Discussion
sections.learningOutcome: Choose a context-sensitive next move in a fresh task, using explicit words and relevance rather than a memorised intervention or guessed motive.
